Thresholds for the validation checks

Source: R/config.R
validation_config.Rd

Defaults mirror ValidationConfig in bdp-model-gate 0.7.0.

Usage

validation_config(
  leakage_ratio = 0.95,
  leakage_min_power = 0.8,
  max_split_overlap = 0.01,
  max_duplicate_fraction = 0.05,
  drift_threshold = 0.25,
  categorical_drift_threshold = 0.15,
  out_of_time_strategies = c("out_of_time", "temporal", "forward_chaining",
    "walk_forward"),
  accepted_validation_strategies = c("out_of_time", "temporal", "forward_chaining",
    "walk_forward", "random_split", "stratified_split", "cross_validation",
    "grouped_split"),
  require_out_of_time_for_high_risk = TRUE
)

Arguments

leakage_ratio

A feature is a suspected leak when its solo power reaches this fraction of the model's own. Used by target_leakage_check().

leakage_min_power

...and only when that power is at least this, on 0-1: one ordinary feature should not explain the target this well.

max_split_overlap

Largest tolerated fraction of validation rows that also appear in the training frame.

max_duplicate_fraction

Largest tolerated fraction of exact duplicate rows within the validation set.

drift_threshold

Largest tolerated standardised mean shift for a numeric feature (difference in means over the training standard deviation). Used by feature_drift_check().

categorical_drift_threshold

Largest tolerated total variation distance, on 0-1, for any other feature. Used by feature_drift_check().

out_of_time_strategies

Values of model_card$validation_strategy that count as a holdout separated in time rather than at random.

accepted_validation_strategies

Every value that field may take. An unrecognised value is flagged rather than accepted, because "holdout" and "out_of_time" are different claims and only one of them is checkable.

require_out_of_time_for_high_risk

TRUE to flag a high-risk use case (see compliance_config()) that was not validated out of time.

Value

A list of class validation_config.

Examples

strict <- validation_config(max_split_overlap = 0, drift_threshold = 0.1)
X <- data.frame(age = c(25, 32, 47, 51))
report <- run_gate(gate_context(X, X_train = X[1, , drop = FALSE]),
                   list(split_overlap_check(strict)))
report$results[[2]]$flag
#> [1] "SPLIT_OVERLAP_RISK"
